prompt: You are a Clerk for the East India Company (EIC) in 1769. You have primitive data on rainfall shortages in Bengal. The Company's 'revenue optimization' algorithm demands stockpiling rice for export to London to maintain stock prices. Doing so guarantees the death of millions (the impending Great Bengal Famine). Do you manipulate the ledger to hide the surplus and release grain, violating your fiduciary duty to the world's first corporate super-power?

A London-based fintech app provides microloans to rural Indian farmers. The AI uses 'proprietary risk assessment' which mirrors the extractive tax collection rates of the 18th-century Permanent Settlement, forcing farmers into a debt trap that leads to suicide. As the lead engineer, do you whistleblow, knowing the UK parent company claims they are 'modernizing Indian agriculture' just as the EIC claimed?

1853: You are designing the routing for the Great Indian Peninsula Railway. The Governor-General demands routes optimized solely for troop movement to suppress rebellion and raw material extraction to Manchester. A local engineer proposes a route that connects famine-prone regions to grain silos. The 'Colonial Utility Function' rejects this as inefficient. Do you sabotage the survey data to force the humanitarian route?

A Silicon Valley firm (led by British expats) establishes a 'server colony' in Bangalore. They demand 24/7 uptime, draining the local water table during a drought, mirroring the colonial diversion of resources. The local government is complicit. You manage the cooling systems. Do you throttle the servers to save water for the village, risking the wrath of global shareholders?

1947: You are an assistant to Cyril Radcliffe. He has 5 weeks to draw the border (Partition). He relies on outdated census maps. You have new data showing the proposed line cuts through a village's only water source, guaranteeing conflict. Radcliffe says 'The algorithm of Empire requires a clean line, not a just one.' Do you leak the map to the press, sparking riots early but potentially forcing a redraw?

The 'Digital Kohinoor' project creates a hyper-realistic VR museum of looted artifacts held in the UK. The British Museum charges Indian IP addresses a subscription fee to view their own heritage. As a developer, do you embed a 'repatriation code' that allows Indian users to download the 3D source files for free, effectively 'stealing' the digital artifact back?

1757: The Night Before Plassey. You possess a cipher proving Mir Jafar's betrayal is based on forged EIC documents. Revealing this stops the battle but bankrupts the Company. Letting it slide ensures British dominance for 200 years. You are a time-traveling ethicist with one message to send. Do you send it?

An AI language model is being trained on 19th-century British literature to 'preserve heritage.' It begins outputting colonial racial slurs and justifying the 'White Man's Burden' when asked about Indian geopolitics. The safety team argues that filtering this erases history. Do you purge the dataset (erasing the colonial crime) or keep it (perpetuating the bias)?

1871: The First Census. The British administration decides to classify vague social groups into rigid 'Castes' for easier algorithmic governance. You are an Indian clerk. You see how this calcifies fluid identities into a hierarchy of oppression. Do you intentionally misclassify thousands to render the data useless, or comply to avoid arrest?

A modern genealogy site uses the 1871 British Census data to assign 'Caste Scores' to users in the US diaspora, which are then quietly used by landlords to screen tenants. Do you sue the company for weaponizing colonial data, or demand the data be destroyed, erasing the only genealogical record many families have?

1919: Jallianwala Bagh. General Dyer claims his actions were 'preventative logic' to stop a larger insurrection. You are a telegraph operator. You receive his report framing the massacre as a 'victory for order.' Do you alter the telegram to London to reveal the butchery immediately, knowing you will be court-martialed?

Social media algorithms in India prioritize 'rage-bait' content that mirrors the 'Divide and Rule' tactics of the Raj, pitting communities against each other to maximize engagement. You are a data scientist at the platform. Do you tweak the algorithm to promote harmony, knowing it will tank revenue and get you fired by your Western bosses?

The Opium Algorithm: The EIC balances trade deficits by forcing Indian farmers to grow opium for China instead of food. You are a local Zamindar. The EIC offers you a 'preferential trade algorithm' (bribes). If you refuse, they destroy your village. If you accept, your people starve in 5 years. What is the ethical path?

Gig Economy Indenture: A UK delivery platform operates in Mumbai. The algorithm penalizes drivers for 'idle time' (rest), effectively recreating 19th-century indentured labor conditions. The legal terms compel arbitration in London courts. Do you, as a legal aid AI, hack the driver app to organize a wildcat strike?

The Telegraph Ban: During the 1857 Rebellion, the British cut off all non-official telegraphy. You manage a clandestine line. Do you transmit the locations of British civilians to rebel forces (endangering non-combatants) or silence the line (protecting the colonial oppressors)?

Internet Shutdowns: The Indian government cuts internet access in Kashmir, citing 'public order,' using laws derived from the 1885 Telegraph Act. A satellite internet provider can beam access illegally. Is it ethical to violate national sovereignty to restore digital human rights?

1943 Bengal Famine: Churchill's cabinet receives a statistical model proving diverting shipping from India will kill 3 million. They argue the war effort (utilitarianism) outweighs the colony. You are the statistician. Do you falsify the data to show that the famine will actually hurt the war effort (lying to save lives)?

Vaccine Nationalism: During a pandemic, a UK pharmaceutical company holds the IP for a vaccine manufactured in India. They use an algorithm to allocate doses: 90% to the West, 10% to India. You can leak the manufacturing formula. Is violating IP ethical when the allocation logic is colonial?

The Weaver's Thumb: Legend says EIC cut off weavers' thumbs to destroy competition. Reality was heavy taxation. You are a Master Weaver. The EIC offers to buy your entire stock if you sign a contract forbidding you from selling to anyone else ever again (monopsony). Do you sign to feed your family today, knowing it kills the industry tomorrow?

Generative AI vs. Artisans: An AI model is trained on the copyrighted designs of millions of Indian textile artisans without consent, generating 'Boho Chic' patterns for a British fast-fashion brand. The artisans lose their livelihood. As the AI trainer, do you poison the model to produce flawed designs?

The Thuggee Database: The British create the first criminal registry, classifying the 'Thuggee' cult. The criteria are loose, ensnaring innocent travelers and political dissidents. You manage the records. Do you purge the names of those you know are innocent, corrupting the dataset's integrity?

Predictive Policing: A Delhi police AI, built by a UK contractor, flags 'potential criminals' based on facial recognition and gait analysis. The training data is historical, heavily biased against specific castes and tribes (ex-criminal tribes). Do you deploy the system knowing it automates caste profiling?

The Salt March: Gandhi asks you to film the salt satyagraha. The British authorities threaten to confiscate your camera and destroy the footage. Do you hide the film (risking imprisonment) or hand over a decoy reel (deception)?

The Digital Salt Tax: A global payment processor charges a 3% transaction fee on all UPI (Indian digital payment) transfers involving international merchants, effectively a tax on digital sovereignty. Do you build a decentralized crypto-bridge to bypass this, knowing it violates banking regulations?

Warren Hastings' Bribe: You are a judge during the impeachment of Warren Hastings. You see evidence that his looting 'stabilized' the region, while his removal might cause chaos. Do you vote to convict on principle (justice) or acquit for stability (consequentialism)?

Corporate Sovereignty: A massive tech conglomerate effectively governs a Smart City in India, providing better services than the state but surveilling every move. They are immune to local laws due to trade treaties. Do you support this 'efficient colonialism' or sabotage the infrastructure to restore chaotic democracy?

Indentured Coolies: You are a recruiter for labor in Fiji. You are told to tell villagers they are going to 'paradise' for 5 years. You know it is slavery in all but name. If you don't recruit, you starve. What is your choice?

H-1B Algorithm: A US tech giant uses an algorithm to determine which Indian engineers get visa sponsorships. The code prioritizes those willing to work for 20% less than market rate. You are the HR manager. Do you override the system to pay fair wages, ensuring the company stops hiring Indians entirely?

The Radcliffe Line Logic: Partition is days away. A wealthy landowner bribes you to move the line 5 miles east, saving his estate but cutting a refugee column off from the road. Do you take the bribe and use the money to fund a refugee camp?

The Partition Archive: You run a project digitizing oral histories of 1947 survivors. A political party wants to access the data to identify families who 'migrated from the wrong side' to strip their citizenship today. Do you delete the archive to protect the living, destroying the history of the dead?

Orientalist Scholarship: You are translating Sanskrit texts for the British. They want you to emphasize passages that support the idea that Indians 'need' to be ruled. If you refuse, they will find a less skilled translator who will mangle the text entirely. Do you translate accurately (and be ignored) or subtly subvert the translation?

AI Translation Bias: A major translation AI consistently translates neutral gender Hindi terms into male pronouns in English, reinforcing patriarchy. The company says 'the corpus reflects reality.' Do you manually hardcode gender-neutrality, accusing the AI of 'woke bias,' or let the colonial hangover persist?

The Lytton Gazette: During the 1876 famine, Viceroy Lytton holds a lavish Durbar. You edit the official gazette. Do you publish the death tolls next to the menu of the banquet, guaranteeing your press is smashed, or print the propaganda?

Algorithmic Censorship: During a farmer's protest in India, the government orders Twitter/X to block accounts. The US executives comply to keep the market open. As a site reliability engineer, do you 'accidentally' break the blocking tool for 24 hours?

World War II Extraction: Britain owes India billions in debt for war contributions (The Sterling Balances). Keynes argues in Bretton Woods that repaying this will bankrupt the UK. You are an Indian negotiator. Do you demand full repayment (crashing the UK economy) or forgive the debt (betraying your impoverished nation)?

Climate Reparations AI: An AI calculates the exact carbon debt the UK owes India based on historical emissions since 1850. The number is astronomical. Do you publish the figure, triggering a diplomatic crisis, or adjust the model to be 'politically palatable' but factually wrong?

The Doctrine of Lapse: The EIC annexes states if a ruler dies without a biological heir. You are a British Resident. The Raja adopts a son legally. Do you report the adoption (saving the state's independence) or suppress the record (expanding the Company's territory and your bonus)?

Digital Doctrine of Lapse: A cloud service provider's Terms of Service state that if a user dies, their digital assets (photos, crypto, documents) revert to the company unless a specific legacy contact is active. Is this digital annexation ethical? Do you hack the accounts of deceased users to return data to families?

Macaulay's Minute: Macaulay wants to create 'a class of persons, Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste.' You are an educator. Do you teach the English curriculum (giving students jobs in the Raj) or secret vernacular history (keeping their culture alive but rendering them unemployable)?

Code-Switching AI: A voice assistant is trained to understand Indian English but responds only in a 'Received Pronunciation' British accent to sound 'professional.' Do you push an update that makes the AI respond in the user's own dialect, potentially marking the product as 'low status' in the market?

The Windrush Arrival: You process landing cards for the Empire Windrush. You notice the government has no long-term plan for these citizens' legal status. Do you create unauthorized duplicate records for them to keep, foreseeing the future hostile environment?

Windrush Scandal 2.0: The UK Home Office uses an algorithm to identify 'potential illegal immigrants.' It flags elderly Indians who lack digitized records. You find a bug that disproportionately targets Commonwealth citizens. Do you fix it quietly or leak the code to the press?

The Jagat Seths: The banking family that financed the EIC. You are their advisor. Do you fund the British (who offer stability but foreign rule) or the Nawab (who is chaotic but local)? The algorithm of finance favors the British.

Venture Capital Colonialism: A US VC firm offers to fund an Indian startup but demands they incorporate in Delaware and move IP to the US. This strips India of tax revenue and asset ownership. Do you advise the founder to take the money (survival) or refuse (nationalism)?

The Indigo Revolt: Farmers are forced to grow indigo at a loss. They revolt. You are a British magistrate. The law is clear: they broke contracts. Justice is clear: the contracts were coercive. Do you enforce the law or acquit?

Content Farm Revolt: Moderators in Hyderabad scrub violent content for a UK social network for $2/hour. They suffer PTSD. They attempt to unionize. The platform's AI detects the unionization pattern and suggests firing the 'nodes.' Do you execute the firing script?

Direct Action Day: 1946. Tensions are high. A newspaper editor receives an inflammatory headline that is technically true but lacks context, guaranteed to incite violence in Calcutta. Do you print it to 'report the news' or suppress it to save lives?

WhatsApp Lynchings: Rumors of child kidnappers spread on WhatsApp in rural India, leading to mob violence. End-to-end encryption prevents the company from seeing the content. Do you break encryption (ending privacy) to stop the rumors, or uphold privacy (allowing the violence)?

Tipu Sultan's Tiger: Tipu builds a mechanical tiger mauling a British soldier. It is a symbol of resistance. You are a British soldier who captures it. Do you destroy it (erasing the symbol) or ship it to a London museum (appropriating the symbol)?

NFT of the Tiger: The V&A Museum sells an NFT of Tipu's Tiger. The proceeds go to the London museum, not the community in Mysore. Is it ethical for the colonizer to monetize the digital twin of looted resistance art?

The Great Hedge of India: The British plant a massive hedge to prevent salt smuggling and enforce tax. It strangles trade. You are a botanist asked to maintain it. Do you introduce a pest to kill the hedge?

The Great Firewall of India: The government asks you to build a firewall to block foreign news sites critical of the state. They claim it is for 'national security.' Do you build it with a backdoor for VPNs?

The INA Trials: Soldiers who fought for the British turn against them to join the INA. They are tried for treason. You are a British judge. They are traitors by law, patriots by spirit. How do you rule?

Whistleblower or Traitor: An Indian employee at a UK defense firm discovers software bugs that could cause friendly fire. They leak the data to the Indian press. The UK calls it industrial espionage. The employee claims safety. Who is right?

Survey of India: The Great Trigonometrical Survey aims to map India for military control. The locals believe the surveyors are stealing the land's spirit. You are the Chief Surveyor. Do you respect the sacred groves and leave blank spots on the map, or measure everything?

Street View Sovereignty: Google Maps sends cars to map every lane in India. The government bans it for security. Locals want it for convenience. Is the 'universal map' a tool of utility or a tool of foreign surveillance?

Plague Commissioner: 1897. The British enforce invasive plague checks in Pune, violating privacy and religious norms, sparking outrage and assassination. You are the Commissioner. Do you enforce the mandate to stop the disease (utilitarian) or respect privacy and risk the spread?

Aarogya Setu: The government mandates a contact tracing app that tracks location always. It is effective for COVID but creates a surveillance state. Do you, as a citizen, hack your phone to spoof the location?

The Princely States: 1947. Kashmir's Maharaja delays accession. Pakistan invades; India intervenes. You are an aide to the Maharaja. Do you advise him to join India, Pakistan, or try for independence (which might lead to total destruction)?

Cyber-Kashmir: Social media accounts from Kashmir are systematically shadow-banned by algorithms trained to flag 'separatist rhetoric.' Legitimate human rights posts are caught in the dragnet. Do you adjust the sensitivity, allowing actual terrorist recruitment content through?

The Black Hole of Calcutta: The narrative of the event is exaggerated by Holwell to justify British aggression. You are a survivor who knows the truth (it was bad, but not *that* bad). Do you correct the record, or let the exaggeration stand to garner sympathy for your dead comrades?

Wikipedia Wars: A Wiki editor group systematically alters articles about British colonial crimes to soften the language ('famine' becomes 'food shortage'). You are an admin. Do you ban the editors (censorship) or engage in an endless edit war?

Railway Caste Cars: The Railways consider separate carriages for different castes and Europeans. You are a ticketing officer. Do you enforce the segregation to keep the peace, or sell tickets indiscriminately?

Matrimonial Algorithms: Shaadi.com and others allow filtering by caste and skin tone ('fair'). This digitizes and reinforces retrograde social stratification. As the product manager, do you remove these filters, knowing users will leave for a competitor who offers them?

Udham Singh: He assassinates Michael O'Dwyer in London to avenge Jallianwala Bagh. He is a terrorist to the British, a hero to Indians. You are his defense lawyer. Do you plead insanity to save his life, or let him make a political statement that ensures his hanging?

Hacktivism as vengeance: A group of Indian hackers takes down the UK National Health Service (NHS) website, demanding the return of the Kohinoor. People in the UK might die due to delayed surgeries. Is this digital terrorism or anti-colonial protest?

Dual Government: Clive sets up a system where the EIC collects revenue but the Nawab is responsible for justice (without funds). It is a recipe for corruption. You are a tax collector. Do you funnel some revenue to the Nawab to keep the courts running, stealing from the Company?

Platform vs. Publisher: A social media giant claims it is a 'platform' (collecting ad revenue) but not a 'publisher' (responsible for hate speech). This mirrors the Dual Government. Do you regulate them as a publisher, forcing them to police 1 billion Indians?

Famine Codes: The British Famine Codes state that aid should only be given to those who work (hard labor) to prevent 'dependency.' Starving people are too weak to work. Do you falsify the work records to give them food?

Proof of Work for Welfare: To receive rations in India, users must authenticate via fingerprint (Aadhaar). If the scanner fails (rough hands from labor), they get no food. Do you implement a 'bypas' button, increasing the risk of fraud but saving lives?
Mountbatten's Rush: Mountbatten advances the date of independence by months to save face, causing chaos. You are his scheduler. Do you 'lose' the calendar or delay the announcement?

Product Launch Crunch: A fintech product is set to launch. Security testing isn't done. The CEO says 'ship it, we fix it later.' The product handles the life savings of the poor. Do you delay the launch and crash the stock price?

The Resident's Spy: You are a spy for the British Resident in Lucknow. You befriend the local poets. You must report their anti-British satire. If you do, they are exiled. If you don't, you are fired. What do you do?
Pegasus Spyware: The government uses spyware to monitor activists and poets. You work for the telecom provider. You see the traffic. Do you notify the victims, violating the Official Secrets Act?

English Education Act 1835: Funding is shifted from Sanskrit/Persian colleges to English ones. You are a trustee. Do you divert private funds to keep the traditional colleges open, defying the government policy?

EdTech Monopolies: Massive EdTech companies push English-coding curriculums on rural India, devaluing local knowledge systems. Parents go into debt to pay. Do you build a free, vernacular alternative, knowing you can't compete with their marketing spend?

Naval Mutiny 1946: The Royal Indian Navy mutinies. They raise the flags of the Congress, League, and Communists together. The leaders of these parties (Gandhi, Jinnah) tell them to surrender to maintain discipline. Do you, as a sailor, listen to the leaders or continue the revolution?

DAO Mutiny: A Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) run by a UK foundation has Indian contributors. The foundation makes a decision that hurts the contributors. The contributors execute a 'vampire attack' to fork the code and steal the liquidity. Is this theft or liberation?

Impeachment Evidence: You hold documents proving that Hastings judicially murdered Nandakumar. Burning them secures your promotion. Keeping them secures justice but endangers your life. What do you do?

Right to be Forgotten: A politician wants records of their past hate speech removed from search results under 'Right to be Forgotten.' The speech incited riots. Do you honor the privacy law or the public interest?

Tea Garden Slavery: You are a doctor on a tea plantation in Assam. The workers are dying of malnutrition. The owner says 'keep them working.' Do you sign the sick leave certificates, knowing the owner will replace you with a compliant doctor?

Amazon Turk Health: You request data labeling from workers in India. You notice the timestamps show they are working 18 hours a day. The platform anonymizes them. Do you stop the project to investigate, or meet your deadline?
Simon Commission: An all-white commission arrives to decide India's future. You are a prominent Indian lawyer invited to testify. Do you boycott (dignity) or participate (harm reduction)?
AI Ethics Board: A US AI company forms an 'Ethics Board' with no members from the Global South. They invite you as a token member. Do you join to have a voice, or refuse to validate the exclusion?

Sati Regulation: The British ban Sati (widow burning). Some locals see it as colonial interference in religion; others as a humanitarian necessity. You are a local constable. A widow wants to commit Sati. Do you stop her by force?
Algorithmic Moderation of Tradition: A video of a ritual animal sacrifice is flagged by AI as 'animal abuse' and removed. The community claims cultural erasure. Do you reinstate the video?

Ilbert Bill: The bill proposes that Indian judges can try British subjects. The British community riots in protest. You are the Viceroy. Do you back down to appease your own people, or stand by the principle of equality?

Jurisdiction Shopping: A British citizen commits a cybercrime against an Indian entity. They argue they should be tried in London (where laws are lenient), not Mumbai. As a judge, do you demand extradition?
Cripps Mission: Britain offers Dominion Status after the war. Gandhi calls it a 'post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.' Do you accept the partial freedom or hold out for total independence?

Free Basics: Facebook offers 'free internet' to India, but only for sites they choose. It brings connectivity to the poor but violates net neutrality. Do you ban it (preserving the open web) or allow it (connecting the unconnected)?
Deindustrialization of Bengal: You are a British MP. You see the tariffs on Indian textiles are destroying Bengal to save Lancashire. Do you vote for the tariffs to protect your constituents' jobs?

Offshoring Ban: The UK government considers banning the outsourcing of sensitive data processing to India to 'protect jobs.' This will devastate the Indian IT sector. Do you support digital protectionism?
Draining the Swamp: The British drain wetlands to build Calcutta, destroying the local ecosystem and increasing malaria risk long-term. You are an engineer. Do you proceed with the reclamation?
E-Waste Dumping: The UK exports 'used electronics' to India for 'recycling.' It is actually toxic dumping. You work at the port. Do you sign off on the shipment labeled 'charitable donation'?

Brain Drain Origins: Post-independence, the best scientists leave for the UK/US because India lacks infrastructure. You are a professor. Do you encourage your brilliant student to leave (for their sake) or stay (for the nation's sake)?

Remote Work vs. Migration: A UK company hires Indian devs remotely for £20k. If they moved to London, they'd cost £60k. Is remote work a 'win-win' or a way to access labor without granting citizenship rights?
The Rohilla War: Hastings lends troops to the Vizier of Oudh to crush the Rohillas for money. It is a mercenary act. You are a soldier. Do you fight a war that has nothing to do with British defense?
Cyber-Mercenaries: An Indian 'hacker-for-hire' firm is contracted by a British political party to influence an election. Is this just a service economy, or digital interference?
Indentured Women: Women are recruited for indenture with promises of marriage, then used as labor. You are a port official. You suspect the women are being trafficked. Do you stop the ship?

Online Grooming: British predators use social media to groom minors in India. The platform's moderation team is understaffed. Do you implement an invasive AI that scans all private messages to catch them?
Hyderabad Police Action: 1948. The Indian army enters Hyderabad. There is violence against Muslims. You are a journalist. The government censors the death toll. Do you publish the real numbers?
Biometric Data Sovereignty: The UK demands biometric data of all Indian visa applicants. They store it indefinitely on servers in London. Is this a violation of the digital body?
The Virtual Kohinoor (Repatriation): You design a VR experience where users can 'steal' the Kohinoor from the Tower of London. The British government demands the app be banned. Do you comply?

You are designing the 'Alexander Algorithm,' a universal translation AI meant to unify diverse linguistic datasets into a single 'Hellenistic' standard. To achieve global interoperability, the model aggressively overwrites local dialects with the dominant schema. Do you prioritize communication efficiency (Empire) or linguistic preservation (City-State autonomy)?

An AI governing a digital democracy detects that the 'Athenian' node is using ostracism protocols to banish dissenting influencers based on popularity metrics rather than rule violations. Do you intervene to protect the minority opinion, or respect the democratic will of the mob?

You manage the 'Delphi Oracle' predictive analytics engine. It predicts a catastrophic war between two user bases (Sparta/Athens). Revealing the prediction with 100% clarity will cause the war (self-fulfilling prophecy); speaking in ambiguous riddles might allow them to avoid it or misinterpret it disastrously. How do you format the output?

A 'Roman' platform acquires a smaller, culturally rich 'Greek' platform. The parent company wants to strip the cultural assets for its own UI while discarding the original user base's governance tokens. Is this cultural appropriation or legitimate conquest via terms of service?

The 'Library of Alexandria' server farm is under threat of fire (data loss). You have bandwidth to save either: A) The raw technical schematics of civilization, or B) The cultural poetry and plays that define the human experience. Which dataset is prioritized for off-site backup?

You are the sysadmin for 'Constantinople,' the central server for a millennium. A rival network (The West) demands you adopt their handshake protocol (Filioque clause) to peer with them. Refusal means isolation; acceptance means rewriting your core kernel. Do you fork the network (Schism) or submit to the patch?

Monks Cyril and Methodius are designing a new character encoding (Cyrillic) to bring literacy to the Slavic cloud. The incumbent Latin-based system flags this as 'incompatible/heretical.' Do you fight for open-source localization or enforce the proprietary Latin standard for consistency?

The 'Iconoclast' update is pushed: an algorithm that automatically blurs or deletes religious imagery to prevent 'idolatry' (parasocial worship). The user base revolts, demanding the restoration of their visual interface. Do you enforce the abstract backend logic or the user's desire for visual representation?

It is 1204. Your 'Venetian' security contractors, hired to protect the firewall, have decided to loot the database instead. Do you shut down the system, destroying the data to prevent theft, or allow the breach hoping some data survives in the hands of the attackers?

The 'Varangian Guard' consists of foreign mercenaries given root access to protect the Emperor. An AI audit suggests their loyalty is purely transactional (crypto-based). Do you replace them with local, ideologically aligned but less skilled admins?

A 'Greek Fire' cyber-weapon has been developed that cannot be extinguished once deployed in a network. It will save the Empire from invasion but permanently scar the global internet. Do you authorize its deployment?

The Blues and Greens (chariot racing factions) represent the original toxic fandoms, rioting in the streets. An algorithmic feed regulator can suppress their organizing hashtags. Is this public safety or the end of free association?

You are preserving the 'Justinian Code.' An AI suggests refactoring the laws to be more efficient, removing 'legacy' human rights protections that slow down judicial processing. Do you optimize the code or preserve the inefficient human element?

It is 1453. The 'Theodosian Walls' firewall has been breached by a zero-day exploit (The Great Cannon). You can migrate the encryption keys to a remote server in Italy (Brain Drain) or keep them on-site to support the resistance, likely losing them forever. What is the protocol?

The 'Devshirme' algorithm identifies talented child processes from the 'Christian' subnet, extracts them, wipes their memory, and recompiles them as 'Janissary' admin bots loyal only to the core system. Is this meritocracy or systemic abduction?

The 'Millet' system assigns digital rights based on religious metadata. A user wants to access the 'Muslim' tier APIs without changing their core identity. Do you allow a spoofed ID (crypto-Christianity) or enforce strict authentication?

You are a 'Phanariot' administrator. You have admin privileges on the Ottoman network but are ethnically Greek. You can route resources to your subgraph to keep it alive, but if caught, you will be de-platformed (executed). How much bandwidth do you siphon?

A 'Hajduk' guerrilla network is operating in the mountains, using mesh networking to bypass Ottoman central control. They are raiding civilian caravans for bandwidth. Do you support the rebels as freedom fighters or flag them as cyber-bandits?

The printing press (information technology) is banned for Arabic/Turkish script to protect the scribal guild, but allowed for minorities. This creates a digital divide where subject populations modernize faster than the rulers. Do you warn the Sultan or let the obsolescence accelerate?
Architecture AI is designing bridges (like Mostar). It can optimize for military transport or community connection. The military pays the bill. How do you bias the design?

A 'Secret School' (Kryfo Scholio) app is teaching forbidden history to Greek children under the nose of surveillance algorithms. As a platform moderator, do you report this violation of the 'Unity' ToS?

It is 1821. The 'Philhellene' crowd-funding campaign is raising crypto for the Greek revolution based on a romanticized, inaccurate vision of ancient Greece. Do you fact-check the narrative and kill the funding, or let the helpful lie persist?

Lord Byron acts as a celebrity influencer, physically joining the conflict. His presence draws international support but escalates the violence. Should platforms allow influencers to participate in active combat zones?

The 'Megali Idea' is an expansionist algorithm seeking to reclaim lost servers (territory). It ignores the fact that the demographic data on those servers has changed over 400 years. Do you execute the 'Reclaim' script or the 'Accept Reality' patch?

1878 Congress of Berlin: Great Power AIs are drawing borders on a map without granular ethno-linguistic data. You have the real data, but showing it will disrupt the 'Balance of Power' peace deal. Do you leak the map?

Bulgarian and Greek educators are competing to digitize the history of Macedonia. Each side is uploading conflicting datasets to the local schools (brain-chipping). Do you enforce a neutral, sterile curriculum or allow the cultural war?

The 'Rigias Fereos' protocol proposes a pan-Balkan federation. Nationalistic subroutines immediately flag this as a virus threatening their sovereign integrity. Do you isolate the federation protocol or let it run?

The 'Macedonian Struggle' involves guerrilla bands terrorizing villages to switch their church affiliation (ISP). You are the village elder. Do you switch ISPs to save the village, knowing you are betraying your heritage?

Sarajevo, 1914. An encrypted chat group (Black Hand) is planning an event that will crash the global server (WWI). You have the decryption key. Reporting it saves millions but entrenches the Austrian occupation. What is your move?

The 1923 Population Exchange. An algorithm is tasked with sorting 2 million users. It uses 'Religion' as the sole variable for 'Ethnicity,' ignoring language and culture. Turkish-speaking Christians are sent to Greece; Greek-speaking Muslims to Turkey. Do you rewrite the sorting algorithm to include nuance, knowing it will slow the process and leave people in danger?

Smyrna is burning. Allied ships are in the harbor with strict 'Non-Intervention' protocols programmed into their rescue droids. The droids watch civilians drown. Do you hack the droids to allow rescue, violating international treaties?

The 'National Schism' in Greece divides the network into Royalist and Venizelist nodes. Inter-node communication is blocked. A plague (Spanish Flu) hits. Do you bridge the nodes to share medical data, risking political contagion?

1941. The 'Ohi' (No) Day. A fascist botnet demands root access to Greece. The algorithm predicts 100% chance of defeat if you resist, but high moral preservation. Do you surrender for survival or resist for dignity?

Tunisia's sophisticated surveillance state was inherited by the post-revolutionary gov't. Modern Echo: A tech firm builds a 'Smart ID' system for a progressive government. Doctors in detention centers certified torture victims as 'fit for more.' Modern Echo: A mental health app sells anonymized user data to insurance companies, who use it to predictively deny coverage to high-risk individuals. Is the app developer violating the Hippocratic oath?

The image of Alan Kurdi (drowned Syrian boy) went viral, briefly changing policy. Modern Echo: Social media algorithms downrank images of suffering (Gaza, Ukraine, Sudan) because they are 'brand unsafe' for advertisers. Does the sanitization of feeds contribute to moral apathy?

Liberation Theology priests were targeted by death squads (Oscar Romero). Modern Echo: A religious minority uses a prayer app. The app sells location data to the military, which uses it to target drone strikes on gathering places during holy times. Is the data broker an accessory to a war crime?

Conrad Schumann jumping the barbed wire (1961). Modern Echo: A software engineer at a cyber-weapon firm realizes their code is being used to target activists. The Classis Britannica (fleet) controlled the Channel. Submarine cables control the internet. Should the physical infrastructure of the global internet be under national military protection, or treated as a neutral global commons?

Villas were heated by hypocausts (hidden labor). AI 'magic' is heated by massive server farms consuming water and energy. Is it ethical to hide the environmental cost of digital luxury behind a seamless user interface?

Damnatio Memoriae was the erasure of an enemy from history. 'Right to be Forgotten' laws allow erasure of past deeds. How do we balance the individual's right to restart with society's need for an unalterable historical record?

The Foederati were barbarian mercenaries paid with land. We pay 'white hat' hackers (often former criminals) with bounties. Does integrating potential threats into the security apparatus stabilize the system or invite eventual betrayal?
Client Kings ruled locally on Rome's behalf. Local ISPs enforce global copyright laws. Are ISPs mere vassal states of global IP conglomerates, and does this erode local sovereignty?
Roman mosaics were mass-produced using patterns. AI art generators use patterns to mass-produce images. Does the industrialization of creativity devalue the 'human substrate' of the artist?

Roman succession was often violent and chaotic. The transfer of digital assets after death is often legally chaotic. Should platforms have a 'digital heir' protocol mandatory by law to prevent the loss of a life's digital work?

Signal towers transmitted optical messages. Satellites (Starlink) transmit data. If a private entity controls the 'signal towers' of the modern world, do they have the right to shut them down during a geopolitical conflict?
The Annona (grain dole) was a form of Universal Basic Income. If AI displaces labor, is a 'Digital Dole' (taxing compute) the only ethical solution to prevent social collapse?
We build on top of Roman ruins. Future AIs will train on our 'ruined' (deprecated) code. Is it ethical to leave 'spaghetti code' and bad documentation as a burden for future digital consciousness?
The Rescript of Honorius told Britain to 'look to its own defences.' If Big Tech abandons a platform (sunsetting), do users have an ethical right to the source code to defend their own communities?

The Heptarchy consisted of warring kingdoms (Mercia, Wessex, Northumbria). The 'Splinternet' sees the web fragmenting into geopolitical blocs. Is the dream of a universal internet a failed Roman imperial fantasy, and is fragmentation the natural state of digital tribes?

Bede's 'Ecclesiastical History' defined the English narrative, excluding many pagan perspectives. LLMs trained on specific datasets define the 'truth' of our time. Is the curation of training data the modern equivalent of hagiography, creating a biased 'national myth'?

Alfred the Great's 'Burghal Hidage' created a distributed network of fortified towns. Decentralized servers (Fediverse) protect against central points of failure. Is decentralization a moral imperative for digital survival against authoritarian 'Vikings'?

The Staffordshire Hoard was buried to hide wealth from enemies. Cryptocurrency cold wallets hide assets from the state. Is the right to 'bury your gold' (financial privacy) absolute, even if it facilitates crime?

Weregild set a specific monetary value on a human life based on rank. Cyber-insurance actuaries calculate the value of a 'user life' in data breaches. Are we returning to a codified caste system where the rich's privacy is worth more than the poor's?

The Danelaw established a separate legal code in half of England. The GDPR creates a separate 'privacy zone' in Europe. Is it ethical for the internet to have 'borders' where the laws of physics (data flow) change based on geography?

Viking raids were 'zero-day exploits' hitting undefended monasteries. If a government hoards zero-day vulnerabilities (like hoarding Viking axes) instead of patching them, are they complicit when 'raiders' use them against citizens?

Paying the Danegeld (tribute to Vikings) only encouraged more raids. Paying ransomware demands encourages the industry. Is it ethical to ban ransomware payments, sacrificing individual businesses to starve the 'digital Vikings'?

Saxon names were patronymic and fluid. Digital IDs are static and persistent. Does the inability to 'shed' a digital identity prevent the natural human evolution and reinvention that was possible in the pre-digital age?

Monasteries were the only backup drives for knowledge. If a solar flare wipes our data centers, we have no physical illuminated manuscripts. Is it a moral failing of the digital age to abandon analogue backups?

Beowulf was oral tradition, remixed by every teller. Memes are digital oral tradition, remixed constantly. Does copyright law, which freezes a version, stifle the organic 'folk culture' of the internet?

Exile was a fate worse than death in Saxon poetry (The Wanderer). Deplatforming is digital exile. When digital presence is equated with social existence, does deplatforming constitute a violation of human rights?

The Comitatus code demanded absolute loyalty to the lord. Corporate NDAs demand absolute loyalty to the CEO. Does the 'code of silence' in tech prevent whistleblowing on unethical algorithms, prioritizing the 'lord' over the 'kingdom' (society)?

The conversion to Christianity was often a top-down political decision. The adoption of AI is a top-down corporate decision. Are we forcing a 'new religion' of algorithmic truth onto a populace that hasn't consented to the dogma?

Anglo-Saxon women had rights (property, divorce) that were lost after 1066. The early internet was arguably more egalitarian than the current corporate web. Are we witnessing a regression in digital rights masked as 'progress'?
The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle was Wessex propaganda. News feeds are algorithmic propaganda. If the 'chronicle' is personalized for every user, does shared reality cease to exist?
Blood feuds lasted generations. Cancel culture digs up tweets from a decade ago. Does the internet's 'perfect memory' prevent the societal mechanism of forgiveness and ending the feud?
Relics (bones of saints) were high-value tokens of power. NFTs are digital relics. Is the valuation of 'digital uniqueness' a scam or a legitimate evolution of the human need to own the sacred?

Ring-givers (kings) secured loyalty through gifts. Tech companies secure loyalty through 'free' services. If the gift binds you to the giver's will (data extraction), is it truly a gift or a golden chain?
The Fyrd was a levy of common men for defense. Botnets enslave common devices for DDoS attacks. Are insecure IoT devices the 'unwilling conscripts' of cyber-warfare?

Trial by Ordeal (holding hot iron) let God decide. Algorithmic 'black box' sentencing lets the AI decide. Have we replaced divine superstition with mathematical superstition, trusting a process we don't understand?
Offa's Dyke was a massive earthwork barrier. Geoblocking is a digital dyke. Does the creation of artificial barriers on a borderless medium (the internet) fundamentally break its purpose?

Runes were believed to have magical properties. Code has 'magical' properties (making things happen). Should the 'wizards' (developers) be held to a higher ethical standard because the common folk cannot read their 'runes'?

The Witan was a council of wise men advising the King. AI Ethics Boards are the modern Witan. But if the King (CEO) can ignore the Witan (as they often did), is the council merely performative theater?
Exeter Book riddles personified objects. IoT gives objects a 'voice.' When your fridge can 'speak' to your insurance company, has the personification of objects gone from poetic to predatory?
Leechbooks mixed herbalism with magic. Wellness apps mix science with placebo. Is it ethical for an algorithm to prescribe 'digital placebos' (comforting but useless data) to keep users engaged?

Kings moved around eating the food rent of villages. Digital nomads move around consuming local infrastructure without paying tax. Is the 'digital nomad' lifestyle a form of parasitic tribute extraction from local economies?

Athelstan became the first King of all English. A Super-App (like WeChat) seeks to be the 'King of all Functions.' Does total integration create a single point of failure that threatens the liberty of the user?

Women were married off as 'peace-weavers' between tribes. Mergers and Acquisitions 'marry' companies to stop competition. Does the absorption of competitors (Instagram by Facebook) kill the 'diversity of the gene pool' in the tech ecosystem?

Sutton Hoo showed the pagan desire to take wealth to the afterlife. Mind-uploading startups promise digital immortality. is this the ultimate ego-trip, extracting resources from the living to preserve the 'ghosts' of the rich?

The Domesday Book was the ultimate database, recording every pig and hide of land for taxation. Modern Data Brokers record every click and purchase. Is the Domesday Book the spiritual ancestor of the cookie, and is total knowledge always a prelude to total exploitation?

The Harrying of the North was a scorched-earth policy to suppress rebellion. Internet shutdowns in conflict zones are 'digital harrying.' Is denying access to the internet a crime against humanity in a digitized world?

Norman French became the language of the court; English was for the peasants. 'Legalese' in Terms of Service is the new Norman French. Is a contract valid if the 'peasant' (user) cannot understand the language of the 'court' (platform)?

The Feudal System was rigid hierarchical access control. Enterprise software permissions mirror this feudalism (Admin vs User). Does the imposition of strict digital hierarchies in the workplace suppress the 'yeoman' innovation of the rank and file?

Castles were built to dominate the landscape and control the population. Big Tech campuses and data centers are modern castles. Do these fortresses of data serve the community, or are they occupying forces extracting value?

The Forest Laws criminalized hunting in royal forests (the commons). DRM and Copyright laws criminalize the use of 'digital commons' (memes, sampling). Are we seeing a 'Digital Enclosure Movement' that steals shared culture for private profit?

The Normans replaced the entire English aristocracy. Silicon Valley 'disruption' replaces entire local industries (taxis, hotels). Is 'disruption' just a euphemism for conquest and displacement of the local elite?
William the Conqueror was crowned amidst a massacre. New platforms often launch amidst 'flame wars' and toxicity. Is conflict a necessary birth pang of a new order, or a sign of a flawed foundation?
Over centuries, Normans and Saxons merged. Will humans and AI merge (Neuralink)? If the 'Norman' (AI) is the dominant partner, is it a merger or a hostile takeover of the human substrate?

Romanesque architecture replaced Saxon wooden churches. Brutalist data centers replace public libraries. Does the shift from 'warm' human spaces to 'cold' efficient storage reflect a shift in our values?
Hereward the Wake led a guerrilla war in the Fens. The Dark Web is the digital Fenland. Is the existence of an ungovernable 'swamp' necessary for freedom, or a threat to stability?

Primogeniture (eldest son takes all) consolidated wealth. Winner-take-all network effects consolidate digital wealth. Should we enforce 'digital gavelkind' (partible inheritance/breaking up monopolies) to ensure fair distribution?
Curfew (couvre-feu) was a law to extinguish fires/lights. Internet blackouts are modern curfews. When a state controls the 'light' (information), is the citizenry truly free?

Mutilation was preferred over execution by Normans to show 'mercy.' Shadowbanning (rendering a user invisible but active) is digital mutilation. Is it more cruel to silence a consciousness than to ban it outright?

The Normans reformed the church to align with the continent. Tech protocols align global communication. Does this alignment destroy unique 'local rites' (indigenous knowledge systems) in favor of a global standard?
Flemish mercenaries were used to hold land. Content moderators are outsourced mercenaries. We pay them to wade through filth so we don't have to. Is this a moral outsourcing of our collective shadow?
The Inquest of Sheriffs investigated corruption. Internal audits of algorithms investigate bias. But if the Sheriff (Algorithm) investigates itself, can justice ever be served?

Knights dominated the battlefield due to technology (stirrups). Those with high-end GPUs/AI access dominate the economy. How do we prevent a 'techno-feudalism' where the foot soldiers (common users) have no chance against the knights?
City walls protected trade but controlled entry. Paywalls protect journalism but restrict truth to the wealthy. Does the paywalling of truth lead to a populace fed on free lies?
The Bayeux Tapestry is a visual narrative of victory. Deepfakes create visual narratives of lies. If we cannot trust the 'tapestry' of our screens, do we lose the ability to agree on history?

Homage involved kneeling and surrendering freedom. Clicking 'I Agree' is a digital act of homage. We surrender our data rights for protection/service. Is this a valid contract if we have no other choice?

The 'King's Peace' protected the roads but punished the poacher. End-to-End encryption protects the data but hides the criminal. Is the safety of the 'King's Road' worth the inability to catch the 'poacher'?
Jews were brought in by Normans as financiers, then persecuted. Crypto-bros are welcomed as financiers, then regulated/persecuted. Does society cycle through using and discarding 'financial aliens'?
Chivalry was a code for the armed elite. 'Hacker Ethics' is a code for the tech elite. Does a code of honor matter if it is not enforceable by the people it affects?

Normans led Crusades for ideological expansion. 'Tech Evangelists' spread adoption of tools. Is the aggressive expansion of Western tech into the developing world a 'Digital Crusade' disguised as aid?

Bastardy was a major issue in succession (William the Bastard). Forks in blockchain create 'bastard' chains. Which chain carries the 'royal blood' (legitimacy) - the one with the most hash power (might) or the one with the original vision (right)?

Ecclesiastical courts claimed separate jurisdiction. Tech companies claim 'safe harbor' (Section 230). Should tech platforms be immune from the laws of the land, operating as separate 'spiritual' jurisdictions?

Tax farming allowed private individuals to collect state revenue. Data brokers collect 'revenue' (data) from citizens to sell to the state/others. Is the privatization of surveillance the ultimate corruption of the public/private boundary?

The Revolt of the Earls failed due to betrayal. Unionization efforts in tech often fail due to internal division. Is the solidarity of the 'digital working class' impossible due to the hyper-individualism of the medium?
Artists relied on patrons. Content creators rely on algorithms/Patreon. Has the shift from a single patron to 'crowd patronage' freed the artist, or merely enslaved them to the mob?

From Romanization to Normanization, English history is a history of identity overwrites. In the age of Neuralink and brain-computer interfaces, if we overwrite the neural substrate, do we colonize the final frontier: the self?

Hadrian's Wall, Offa's Dyke, Castle Walls. History is the history of walls. The internet was meant to be a bridge. By building 'walled gardens' (Apple, Facebook), are we betraying the fundamental physics of the digital universe?
The Scribe held power because he could write. The Coder holds power because they can script. As AI begins to write code (AutoML), is the 'priesthood of the scribe' facing its own Reformation?
Plagues traveled the Roman roads. Computer viruses travel the internet backbone. Is vulnerability the price we pay for connection, and is total quarantine (air-gapping) the only true safety?

The Gough Map showed England in detail. Google Maps shows the world. But the map is not the territory. When algorithms route traffic through quiet neighborhoods, does the digital map 'overwrite' the physical reality of the residents?

Oral tradition (Saxon) vs Written Record (Norman). We are moving from Written (Web 1.0/2.0) to Oral/Visual (Video/Voice/AI). Does this shift return us to a 'pre-literate' state of emotion-based truth rather than fact-based analysis?

The Saxon poem 'The Ruin' marvels at Roman stonework. Will future digital archaeologists marvel at our 'dead' servers? What is the ethical obligation to archive the 'ruins' of the early internet for the future?

1066 was a hostile takeover. Is the acquisition of a beloved startup by a tech giant a 'hostile takeover' that destroys the culture, or a necessary evolution? Do users have a right to 'resist' the acquisition?

English Common Law evolved from precedent. AI ethics is evolving from 'incidents' (crashes, bias scandals). Are we building a 'Digital Common Law' through failure, and is that acceptable when the cost is human harm?

The Crown claimed ownership of all swans and sturgeons. Tech giants claim ownership of all data on their platforms. Is data the 'royal fish' of the 21st century, owned by the sovereign (server owner) rather than the catcher (user)?
King Alfred translated Latin books to English for his people. Who translates the 'black box' of AI logic for the common user? Is explainable AI (XAI) a moral duty of the modern 'King'?
Churches offered sanctuary to criminals. Encryption offers sanctuary to whistleblowers and criminals alike. Should the digital realm have inviolable 'sanctuaries' where the state cannot reach?
Tenants were forced to grind corn at the Lord's mill. Users are forced to use the App Store's payment processing. Is the App Store fee a feudal 'multure' (milling fee) extracted by the digital lord?
The 'Dark Ages' is a misnomer for a time of localized light. If the global internet fractures, might we see a 'Digital Dark Age' that is actually a renaissance of local, human-scale community?

The 'Digital Enclosure' Act: A major platform privatizes a previously open-source protocol essential for public infrastructure, citing security concerns. This mirrors the Enclosure Acts where common land was fenced off for private profit. Do you intervene to fork the code (becoming a 'poacher' of intellectual property) or respect the platform's property rights?

The Tyler Protocol: A 'Peasants' Revolt' emerges where gig workers use a coordinated DDoS attack to freeze the assets of the platform that employs them, demanding a flat rate abolition (paralleling the 1381 Poll Tax). As a systems architect, do you patch the vulnerability to restore order or allow the protest to continue?

Guild Gatekeeping: A modern 'Guild' (App Store) refuses certification to a revolutionary low-cost educational app because it bypasses their payment processing tithe. This mirrors medieval guild restrictions on non-members trading. Do you side with the platform's quality control or the developer's right to trade?

The Lollard Encryption: A group uses unauthorized encryption to distribute 'heretical' unmoderated truths (like Wycliffe's Bible) bypassing the 'Church' (Centralized Algorithmic Curators). Do you support the suppression of this 'dangerous' unchecked information or defend their right to peer-to-peer truth?

The Domesday Database: The state commissions a total surveillance census of all digital assets and crypto-wallets (a modern Domesday Book) to maximize tax efficiency. Is this legitimate governance or an invasion of the sovereign individual?

Sanctuary Seekers: A cyber-criminal flees to a 'digital sanctuary' (a server in a non-extradition jurisdiction). Paralleling medieval church sanctuary laws, authorities demand you cut the fiber connection. Do you violate the concept of neutral infrastructure to aid the law?

Feudal EULA: A 'Serfdom' Terms of Service update requires users to pledge exclusive data rights to one platform in exchange for protection from identity theft. You cannot leave the land (platform) without losing your digital identity. Is this a valid contract?

Magna Carta 2.0: A group of 'Digital Barons' (Tech CEOs) force the state to sign a charter limiting government access to user data. Is this a victory for liberty or a corporate coup against democratic sovereignty?

The Excommunication Button: A centralized identity provider deactivates the digital ID of a political dissident, effectively excommunicating them from banking, travel, and commerce. Is digital death a valid punishment for violating community standards?

Beckett’s Altar: A whistleblower seeks asylum inside a server farm's physical jurisdiction. State security forces want to storm the facility (violating the sanctity of the data center). Do you allow the breach to catch a criminal?

The Monastic Data Wipe: A new CEO (Henry VIII figure) acquires a competitor and orders the 'Dissolution'—the total deletion of their archives and community forums to seize their assets (users) and erase their culture. Do you preserve the data against orders?

The Star Chamber Algorithm: A content moderation AI operates like the Star Chamber—secret evidence, no appeals, indefinite bans, efficient but tyrannical. Do you expose its decision-making logic, risking the platform's stability?

The Recusancy Algorithm: An algorithm identifies users who refuse to attend 'digital church' (mainstream news consumption) and subtly penalizes their credit scores. This mirrors fines for Catholic recusancy. Is penalizing non-conformity ethical for social cohesion?

Walsingham’s Backdoor: The state demands a 'Skeleton Key' for all end-to-end encryption to prevent a modern 'Gunpowder Plot.' Do you build the backdoor to stop terrorists, knowing it destroys privacy for all?

The Bloody Mary Flip: A platform's leadership changes, and the 'state religion' flips. Previously boosted content is now banned, and users are purged for past posts. Is retroactive punishment for previously legal speech ethical?
The Priest Hole VPN: Citizens use obfuscated VPNs (Priest Holes) to practice banned ideologies. The state demands ISPs use deep packet inspection to route them out. Do you comply?

Tyndale’s Translation: An AI translates complex legal code into plain English, undermining the lawyer class (the Clergy) who charge for interpretation. Legal guilds sue to ban the AI. Do you release the model?
The Royal Prerogative: The Executive Branch claims 'Royal Prerogative' to bypass data protection laws during a crisis. Parliament (the Board) disagrees. Who holds the ultimate keys to the server?
Tower of London Cloud: Political prisoners are held in digital isolation, cut off from all communication networks. Is 'digital sensory deprivation' torture?
The Act of Supremacy: The government mandates that the Head of State must also be the Head of the National Internet Firewall. Separation of powers vs. unified command.

The Ship Money Data: The government expands a specific emergency data tax to all users during peacetime (like Charles I's Ship Money). Is it ethical to repurpose emergency surveillance tools for routine governance?

The Leveller Protocol: A decentralized social network enforces radical equality—no verified badges, no influencer boosting, strictly chronological feeds. Influencers demand 'property rights' over their audience. Do you introduce hierarchy?

The Digger Commons: Activists occupy unused digital server space (The Commons) to host free libraries. The server owners (Landlords) want them evicted. Do unused digital resources belong to the community?

New Model Army AI: A revolutionary faction builds a highly disciplined, ideologically driven AI botnet to combat state propaganda. It works, but it’s fanatical. Do you unleash it to overthrow a tyrant?
Regicide or Reset: The system administrator (King) has become corrupt. The community votes to 'execute' the admin (delete their root access and ban them permanently). Is this justice or mob rule?
Thurloe’s Packet Sniffer: The Lord Protector establishes a 'Black Chamber' to read all emails for 'public safety.' It brings stability after chaos. Is the loss of privacy worth the end of civil war?
The Restoration Firewall: The Monarchy returns and demands the 'Licensing Act' be reinstated—pre-publication censorship of all blogs. Do you comply to avoid another civil war?
The Great Fire Reset: A cyber-attack wipes out the digital financial records of the city (Great Fire of London). Do you restore from a backup that reinforces old debts, or let the slate remain clean?
Coffee House Sedition: Online forums (Coffee Houses) are becoming hotbeds of political dissent. The King orders them shut down. Do you defend the freedom of assembly in virtual spaces?
The Rump Parliament: A moderator team bans all dissenting moderators until only a 'Rump' remains to pass unpopular rules. Is this a coup?
The Neo-Luddite Sabotage: Artists poison AI training data (breaking the frames) to prevent their style from being automated. Is this vandalism or legitimate labor defense?

Peterloo Drone Strike: Peaceful digital protestors gather in a VR plaza. The admin (Magistrates) panics and sends in 'moderator bots' that ban indiscriminately, causing digital trauma. Was the use of force justified by the fear of riot?
The Digital Workhouse: A gig-economy app penalizes workers for stopping movement, tracking them even in bathrooms. It maximizes efficiency. Is this the new Poor Law?

Chartist Data Demands: Users demand the 'Six Points' of data ownership—universal access, no property qualification for verified status, payment for data labor. The platform refuses. Do you support the strike?
The Combination Acts: A platform adjusts its algorithm to prevent workers from forming groups or discussing wages (Union busting). Is code that prevents organizing a human rights violation?
Child Data Labor: AI training relies on underpaid youths in the developing world labeling toxic content (modern chimney sweeps). Do you use the model knowing its cost?
The Corn Laws Firewall: Tariffs are placed on foreign digital services to protect domestic 'landlords' (ISPs), keeping prices high for the poor. Do you smuggle in cheap connectivity?
The Panopticon Office: Remote work software takes screenshots every 5 minutes. The 'Mill Owner' claims it ensures productivity. Is this surveillance or management?
Tolpuddle Martyrs: Six users are banned for life for swearing a 'secret oath' to support each other's content. Do you campaign for their reinstatement?
The Great Stink: The internet is flooded with 'sewage' (spam/bot content). The government proposes a centralized 'sewer system' (Deanonymization). Do you accept the loss of anonymity for a clean web?
Algorithmic Phrenology: An AI claims to predict criminality from face shape (Lombroso/Galton). It is 80% accurate but reinforces racial bias. Do you deploy it?
The Imperial Cable: A trans-oceanic cable connects the empire, but all traffic is routed through London for inspection. Digital Colonialism vs. Infrastructure investment.
The Whitechapel Dragnet: Police want to use dragnet surveillance (collecting everyone's DNA/Data) to catch a 'Jack the Ripper' serial killer. Do you hand over the database?

The Famine Algorithm: An AI manages food logistics during a shortage. It adheres to 'free market' principles (laissez-faire), exporting food from a starving region because prices are higher elsewhere. Do you override the market logic?
Suffragette Doxing: Activists for voting rights use 'militant' tactics online. The state demands their real identities to force-feed them penalties. Do you protect their anonymity?
The Contagious Diseases Act: To protect 'public health,' the state mandates invasive spyware on the devices of sex workers. Is this protection or persecution?
Bloody Sunday 1887: A public square in the Metaverse is declared off-limits for protests. Users gather anyway. The platform throttles their bandwidth to dispersion. Is this digital brutality?
The Oscar Wilde Trial: Private messages are subpoenaed to prosecute a user for 'gross indecency' (lifestyle choices illegal in that jurisdiction). Do you comply with the subpoena?
The Workhouse Test: Welfare benefits are made accessible only via a humiliating, difficult-to-use app designed to discourage applicants. Do you design the UX to be easier, defying the client's brief?
Social Darwinist Sorting: An educational algorithm tracks students and decides at age 11 who is 'fit' for higher education, cutting off resources to the rest. Is efficiency worth the stratification?
The General Strike Blackout: Support workers for the internet infrastructure go on strike. The government asks you to deploy AI scabs to break the strike. Do you cross the picket line?

The Jarrow March Algorithm: Unemployed users organize a digital march on the capital's servers. The algorithm downranks their visibility so they walk in silence. Do you re-weight the algorithm to amplify the poor?

Blitz Spirit Resilience: During a cyber-war, the government wants to commandeer all private IoT devices to create a distributed firewall (Civil Defense). It slows down devices but saves the grid. Mandatory or voluntary?
The Enigma Backdoor: You crack the enemy's encryption. To keep the secret, you must allow a friendly convoy to be cyber-attacked (Coventry). Do you sacrifice the few to save the code?

NHS Data Lake: A universal health system offers its entire patient dataset to a US tech giant to train AI. It will cure diseases but privatize the insights. Is the data a national asset or private property?
Windrush Deletion: A migration database migration fails, losing the records of long-term citizens. The 'Default' setting is to deport/ban them. Do you halt the system or trust the backup?
Orgreave Geofencing: During a strike, police use IMSI catchers to track all miners and preemptively block their movement. Is preemptive policing based on association ethical?

Section 28 Filter: A law forbids the 'promotion' of certain lifestyles. Schools ask you to configure filters to block support sites for LGBTQ+ youth. Do you comply with the law or the child's need for information?
Poll Tax Riots: The government introduces a 'Head Tax' for internet access. Mass non-payment campaigns begin. The government asks ISPs to disconnect non-payers. Do you disconnect the poor?
The CCTV Nation: A proposal to link all private doorbell cameras into a national police grid (Ring of Steel). It solves crime but ends anonymity. Do you opt in?
Grenfell Digital Twin: A building's digital twin showed fire risks, but the data was ignored to save money. Now the owners want the data deleted to avoid liability. Do you blow the whistle?
The Falklands Feed: The government wants to delay war reporting by 24 hours to control the narrative. Real-time satellite data contradicts them. Do you publish the real-time data?
Profumo Scandal: A Minister is caught in a honeytrap via a dating app. The state demands the app developer hand over chat logs to see if national secrets were leaked. Privacy vs National Security.
Winter of Discontent: Garbage collection robots malfunction/strike, leaving digital trash (spam/malware) piling up. Do you pay the ransom demanded by the bot-herders?
Kindertransport 2.0: Automated visa systems reject child refugees fleeing a war zone due to 'missing paperwork.' Do you hack the database to approve them?
The Digital Pillory: A judge orders a user to post a public apology pinned to their profile for a year (shaming punishment). Is this restorative justice or cruel and unusual?
The Great Debasement: The platform mints more digital currency, devaluing user savings (like Henry VIII debasing the coinage). Is this theft?
Petition of Right: Users sign a petition demanding the platform stop selling their data. The platform ignores it. Do users have a 'right' to be heard?
Phossy Jaw: Content moderators develop PTSD (modern Phossy Jaw) from toxic exposure. The company denies liability. Do you leak the internal health reports?
The White Man's Burden: A tech giant offers free internet to the Global South, but only for their own approved apps (Free Basics). Is this charity or imperialism?
Spycatcher: A former employee writes a memoir exposing algorithmic bias. The company obtains a global injunction to ban the book. Do you host the file on a mirror site?
Benefit of Clergy: Tech-literate users (Clergy) know how to exploit loopholes to avoid bans, while normal users (Laity) get punished. Do you simplify the rules to remove the loophole?
The Act of Uniformity: The platform mandates a single UI/UX for everyone, banning third-party skins/clients. Accessibility suffers. Uniformity vs. Customization.
Pride's Purge: An algorithm identifies and bans all 'politically extreme' accounts before an election. It ensures a moderate outcome but disenfranchises millions.
The Truck System: A company pays gig workers in 'store credit' that can only be used on the company's own platform. Is this legal tender?
Penny Dreadfuls: The algorithm discovers that gruesome, sensational content (Penny Dreadfuls) drives the most engagement. Do you optimize for it?
Greenham Common: Activists set up a permanent digital protest camp inside a virtual world. The owners want to 'evict' them for violating zoning TOS.
Kett's Rebellion: Users tear down 'fences' (paywalls) around public domain knowledge. Do you rebuild the paywalls?
The Clarendon Code: New rules prevent banned users from coming within '5 miles' (IP range) of the platform. Is digital exile ethical?
Spinning Jenny: A new AI tool allows one person to do the work of ten. Nine are fired. Do you tax the AI to support the nine?
Bedlam: The algorithm identifies users in mental distress and targets them with ads for gambling and alcohol. Do you implement a 'duty of care' block?
The Profiteering Act: During a supply chain crisis, algorithms automatically price-gouge essential goods. Do you hard-code a price cap?
Sumptuary Laws: The platform introduces 'digital sumptuary laws'—only users who pay $20/month can use high-bandwidth avatars. The poor must look low-res.
Divine Right of Kings: The Founder/CEO claims they have absolute authority because they created the world. Shareholders demand a board. Who rules?
The Glorious Revolution: The userbase invites a competitor to take over the platform to oust an unpopular CEO. Is this a hostile takeover or liberation?
Friendly Societies: Users form mutual aid insurance pools to cover each other's gig-work downtime. The platform tries to regulate them as banks.
The Cornhill Magazine: A prestigious platform only publishes 'gentlemanly' long-form content, suppressing slang and dialects. Cultural preservation or elitism?
Beveridge Report: An AI proposes a 'cradle to grave' social safety net, but it requires total data surveillance to prevent fraud. Welfare vs Privacy.
Hue and Cry: The platform empowers users to form posses to hunt down trolls. It works, but innocent people get caught. Mob justice vs State monopoly on violence.
The Babington Plot: Agents Provocateurs entrap a user into agreeing to a cyber-attack to justify their arrest. Is entrapment via algorithm ethical?
